newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly Republicans see more revs in FY 1998.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly Republicans see more revs in FY 1998.

text.p: New York State Assembly Republicans said they looked for the state to collect an extra $376 million of revenues in the 1998 fiscal year, bringing the total windfall to almost $1.24 billion.

The Republicans, who are the minority party in the Assembly, noted that there is a $373 million unallocated surplus from fiscal 1997, which ended on March 31, and $490 million of extra funds that Gov. George Pataki identified at the start of the new fiscal year on April 1.

The Assembly's minority party said it relied on recently updated data on the U.S. and New York State economies from forecasters DRI/McGraw-Hill, which is based in Lexington, Massachusetts, the state's fiscal 1997 results, and a report by the Ways and Means Committee of the Assembly GOP.
That report predicted that most of the extra windfall will come from personal income taxes, with robust growth in corporate profits pushing up business tax collections.
The legislature and Republican governor had until March 10 to agree on how big the state's revenues would be in fiscal 1998, a deadline they missed.
They also failed to make the April 1 deadline for a budget, a problem the Assembly said was due to the house's majority Democrats.

Still, Assembly Republican Leader Thomas Reynolds of Springville said a proposal by the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, to thrash out the issues in conference might offer a way to resolve the statemate. This would require the Republican-led Senate to approve its own version of a budget, which this year it has not been willing to do.

"I'm encouraged by the Speaker's recent epiphany on Conference Committees and, if he's truly serious, then we should immediately begin work to hammer out a final agreement on available revenues," he said, in prepared remarks.
